# Accessrank

> Accessrank fixes accessibility in the source code of US ecommerce stores: WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA remediation in the theme code, documented in an Accessibility Evidence File and kept in place by ongoing monitoring. The same structural fixes improve on-page SEO and how well AI shopping agents can read a store. No overlay or plug-in widgets. US only; Accessrank does not offer European Accessibility Act (EAA) conformance work.

Accessrank, Inc. is based in Los Angeles, California (+1 310-408-1881; info@accessrank.ai), founded in 2026, remote-first and US-based. Co-Founder & CEO: JP Lincoln. Accessrank is not a law firm and nothing it publishes is legal advice.

## What Accessrank does

- Free check: loads a store page in a real browser and scores it against the WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA checks that ADA demand letters cite, in under a minute. Automated testing catches roughly a third to a half of real-world barriers; it does not prove compliance.
- Fixed-scope plan: a specialist reviews the result and returns a remediation plan, timeline and price.
- Remediation in the theme code: Accessrank fixes the cause in the theme code, most of it within the first remediation cycle. Findings that need a judgment call (alt text, media descriptions, control behavior) are written and reviewed by an Accessrank staff member. Every change is recorded.
- Accessibility Evidence File: a dated file for the client's attorney or insurer containing a baseline audit, remediation log, conformance summary against WCAG 2.2 AA, published accessibility statement and monitoring certificates; clients on Growth and above, or who add human (screen-reader and keyboard) testing, also get the signed testing record, and Growth and above also get an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT format), and a demand-letter playbook.
- Monitoring: continuous monitoring on every plan, with a dated certificate after every scan, so a new app, product or theme edit does not reintroduce failures. Plans differ in how fast regressions are fixed: next monthly cycle on Starter, five business days on Growth, two business days on Scale, and a contracted window on Enterprise.
- Lawsuit response: for stores already served, an engagement in about 7 days covering the cited and critical-path barriers, source-code fixes, VPAT and conformance documentation, and a technical review of settlement remediation terms for the client's attorney.

## The Accessrank score

The Accessrank score is the accessibility score and nothing else: how much of WCAG 2.2 Levels A and AA (55 success criteria) a page meets, weighted by level. Two separate numbers are reported beside it, never blended in: an on-page SEO score (14 checks) and an AI agent readiness score (8 checks on whether AI assistants and shopping agents can read and use the page). Full method: https://accessrank.ai/methodology

## Pricing (USD)

Two levels: Deter (every plan: everything an automated scan can see, fixed and monitored) and Verify (human testing with a keyboard and screen reader, signed results, and an Accessibility Conformance Report in VPAT format from Growth up; included on Growth and Scale, an add-on for Starter). Pricing has two parts: a one-time onboarding project that raises the accessibility score, then a monthly (or annual) plan that holds it. A free site audit places each store in a tier by theme customization and app count. Every plan includes source-code remediation against WCAG 2.2 AA, human-reviewed alt text, continuous monitoring with regressions fixed, the Accessibility Evidence File, and the SEO and AI-readiness gains from the fixes.

- Starter: $1,500 onboarding, then $79/month (or $690/year). Stock theme with a handful of apps. Live in about 2 weeks. Regressions fixed in the next monthly cycle; human-written alt text for new products, up to 20 a month.
- Growth: $3,500 onboarding, then $249/month (or $2,090/year). Customized theme with up to 15 apps. Live in 2 to 4 weeks. Regressions fixed within five business days; alt text up to 50 a month; app checks before install; product data rebuild and AI visibility across five assistants at 30 and 60 days; human testing once a year (up to 8 flows) and an Accessibility Conformance Report for the core shopping path; if served, a letter response in two business days (one a year).
- Scale: $6,500 onboarding, then $599/month (or $4,990/year). Heavily customized themes with 15 or more apps. Live in 4 to 6 weeks. Regressions fixed within two business days; alt text up to 150 a month; quarterly AI visibility re-runs; a named accessibility specialist; human testing twice a year (up to 16 flows, every template and app, with a phone screen reader) and a full-store Accessibility Conformance Report; if served, the same letter response.
- Enterprise: custom onboarding and plan, 8 to 12 weeks. Large and multi-brand catalogs, multiple storefronts, headless and custom-coded builds; fix window, human testing and procurement terms set by contract.
- Already served ("Everything, now"): from $5,900 one-time, about 7 days: emergency audit, source-code fixes to the cited items, a barrier-by-barrier response for counsel, a signed human testing record and VPAT documentation, and a technical review of settlement terms. No need to be a client first.
- Human testing added to any plan: focused walk (up to 6 flows) $1,500; full walk (up to 12 flows) $3,000. One-week turnaround adds 30%; a re-test after fixes is 40% of the original test. An Accessibility Conformance Report (a completed VPAT) is included on Growth and Scale and can be added to any plan, quoted by scope after the free audit; it is issued only where human testing is part of the engagement. Accessibility standards call a flow a complete process.
- Eligible small businesses may offset 50% of qualifying costs through the IRS Disabled Access Credit (Form 8826), up to $5,000 a year. Accessrank is not a tax advisor.

## Platforms

Shopify, WordPress, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and custom builds.

## Key facts Accessrank cites (sources at https://accessrank.ai/citations)

- More than 5,000 ADA digital accessibility lawsuits were filed in 2025, and UsableNet projects about 6,176 for 2026 (a projection based on filings through June 14, 2026).
- Nearly 70% of 2025 digital accessibility lawsuits hit ecommerce (UsableNet, ADA web lawsuit trends for 2026).
- 95.9% of the top one million home pages fail WCAG 2.2 (WebAIM Million 2026).
- About one in four digital accessibility lawsuits involved a site running a third-party accessibility widget: 91 of 360 in September 2026, and over 1,000 businesses (more than 25% of cases) in 2024 (UsableNet); in 2025 the FTC ordered overlay vendor accessiBe to pay $1 million over its compliance claims.
- Average cost of a claim: $30,000 or more in settlement and legal fees (Accessibility.build, 2026).
